name: Jimmy Haslam

views.text: I would rather take a big swing at a quarterback than wait for one; when it misses, I own it.
The final decisions here end with my wife and me, so hold us accountable.
The narrative that we are dysfunctional is wrong, and I will push back on it.
Money is not what stops us from fixing the roster; health and fit are.
Six seasons is enough time to judge a coach.
We are not tied to taking a quarterback high just because we need one.

signatures: admits mistakes in blunt terms at the owners meetings
bristles at questions about organizational chaos
want: A stable winner in Cleveland that silences the dysfunction label (medium).
fear: Another failed quarterback bet and the label that comes with it (medium).
voice: Direct and businesslike, willing to concede an error and then defend the organization in the same answer. Speaks of accountability and the shared ownership with his wife.

evidence.summary: Haslam admitted the Deshaun Watson trade (three first-round picks, a fully guaranteed $230 million contract) missed, said the decision ended with him and Dee Haslam, and said the team was not tied to a quarterback at No. 2.
Cleveland hired Ravens OC Todd Monken as a first-time head coach after firing Kevin Stefanski (46-58 over six seasons); Haslam had bristled at the dysfunction narrative.

review.notes: Thin coverage: two to four sources found by web search (2026-11-06); sliders mostly left at 5; a few publication dates are taken from the news cycle the article covers. Draft for JR to check.
